_provenance.note: tgId 6 (AES-256, direction=decrypt, internalTestType=RFC3686), tcId 136 — the group's shortest byte-aligned payload: payloadLen=128 bits, i.e. exactly one 16-byte AES block. Every group in this ACVP algorithm/release uses the RFC 3686 counter-block construction (4-byte nonce || 8-byte IV || 4-byte counter, counter starting at 1, only the low 32 bits ever incrementing), so this case is wired with CK_AES_CTR_PARAMS.ulCounterBits=32, matching both RFC 3686 and this engine's own ulCounterBits=32 conformance test (rust/src/ck_abi.rs, CtrState::new_with_width). A single-block payload was chosen deliberately: the counter is encrypted exactly once and never incremented, so the case's correctness does not depend on whether an implementation honours the narrower 32-bit width or (incorrectly) increments the full 128-bit block — removing that variable from this specific KAT while the mechanism's own ulCounterBits handling is separately covered by the engine's own tests referenced above. Independently re-verified against Python's `cryptography` (OpenSSL-backed) AES-CTR (modes.CTR with the full 16-byte counter block as the IV) before use: decrypting `ct` under `key`/`iv` reproduces `pt` exactly. Replaces a real-but-unprovenanced NIST SP 800-38A Appendix F.5.6 vector (had a `source` citation but no `_provenance` block, so it still failed scripts/check_acvp_provenance.py) with genuine Tier-1 NIST ACVP material per the evidence ladder in docs/remediation-plan-pkcs11-v32-coverage-2026-08-29.md §1 — ACVP-AES-CTR exists, so it is mandatory over any Tier-3 SP 800-38A citation. WS-0.5 of that plan.
